entries.title: A setting declared without its description, unit, admissible text or check is not constructible
entries.purpose: the guarantee is supposed to be mechanical, not a convention — a declaration that omits its description must fail at import, not lint clean and ship undescribed
entries.body: Declare a setting supplying only a default value and nothing else. The declaration raises `TypeError`, and it raises when the module is imported rather than when the setting is first read. The same holds when any one of description, unit, admissible text or check is omitted while the others are supplied, and when any of them is passed positionally rather than by keyword.

entries.title: A setting whose description, unit or admissible text is blank or whitespace is rejected at construction
entries.purpose: required-keyword-argument is satisfied by `description=""`, which is how an undescribed setting gets past the first guard; the unit is the field that gets the empty string, since dimensionless tempts one
entries.body: Declare a setting supplying every descriptive argument but with an empty string for the description. Construction raises `ValueError`. The same holds for a string of only whitespace, and independently for the unit and for the admissible text. A dimensionless setting states a unit rather than leaving it empty.

entries.title: A declared setting's default and its full declaration record are both recoverable from the dataclass field
entries.purpose: this is the whole coupling the legend projection rests on — if the record is stored anywhere but on the field, every projection has to be told about settings separately, which is the second copy the slice exists to prevent
entries.body: Declare a dataclass with one field declared as a setting. The field's default is the value that was declared as the default, so constructing the dataclass with no arguments yields that value. Reading the field's declaration metadata yields the declaration record, and its description, unit, admissible text, check and provisional mark are the ones that were supplied. The check is callable and answers for a value as it was defined to.

T\u00b730.title: Every artifact must be intelligible to someone arriving with no prior context
Provisionally taken decisions must be revisable without rewriting what was built on them
A configuration explains itself to a reader, including the settings that were left at their defaults
A setting's meaning, unit and admissible values are declared where the setting is declared, and every reader-facing explanation is projected from those declarations
`dark/config/declare.py` is the declaration primitive: `setting()` wraps `dataclasses.field` and a setting without description, unit and admissible values is not constructible
T\u00b730.body:
Module: `dark/config/declare.py`. Stdlib only — `dataclasses`, `typing`. No third-party dependency: Python 3.12 dataclass field metadata already carries arbitrary declaration data, so a settings framework (pydantic, attrs, dynaconf, hydra) buys nothing this project needs and costs a dependency, a schema DSL and a second way to be wrong.

Two public names.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Setting:
    description: str      # what this controls, one sentence, reader-facing
    unit: str             # "m", "s", "Hz", "rad", "1" for dimensionless — never empty
    admissible: str       # reader-facing admissibility, e.g. "> 0", "in [0, 1]"
    check: Callable[[object], bool]   # the machine-checkable form of `admissible`
    provisional: Provisional | None = None

def setting(
    default: object,
    *,
    description: str,
    unit: str,
    admissible: str,
    check: Callable[[object], bool],
    provisional: Provisional | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Returns dataclasses.field(default=default, metadata={"dark": Setting(...)})."""
```

The return annotation is `Any` deliberately — the standard idiom that lets a `field()` sentinel stand where the field's own type is annotated, and the only spelling mypy `strict` accepts without a plugin.

**Not-constructible, mechanically.** All five descriptive arguments are keyword-only and have no defaults, so `setting(3.0)` is a `TypeError` at import. `Setting.__post_init__` additionally raises `ValueError` on an empty or whitespace-only `description`, `unit` or `admissible`. A·02 asks that introducing a setting without its description be impossible rather than discouraged; a required keyword argument plus a constructor guard is the whole of that, and it costs four lines.

**`admissible` and `check` are the same fact in two forms and that duplication is deliberate**, because one is for a reader and one is for the resolver, and no mechanism in stdlib derives readable prose from a predicate. The pairing is kept adjacent in one call so they are edited together; nothing projects one from the other.

**Sequence-valued settings are tuples.** A frozen dataclass default must be immutable, and a tuple default needs no `default_factory`, so `default_factory` is not a parameter of `setting()`. If a mutable default ever becomes genuinely necessary, it is added then.

Ordering note: `declare.py` imports nothing else in this package except `Provisional`, which lives in the same module. Everything else in the slice imports it. No same-layer edge records that — an edge into this slice would have to be an emission, and a slice does not emit into itself.

tests/test_config.py.title: A provisional mark is not constructible without both a claim and the condition that would reverse it
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the revisit condition is the half that gets left off — the claim is the interesting sentence to write and the condition is the one that makes the mark actionable, so the guard has to cover both and cover whitespace
tests/test_config.py.body: Construct a provisional mark with a claim and a blank revisit condition. Construction raises `ValueError`. The same holds for a whitespace-only revisit condition, for a blank claim with a revisit condition supplied, and for both blank. A mark with both non-empty constructs and carries them unchanged.

tests/test_config.py.title: A provisional mark cannot be mutated after construction
tests/test_config.py.purpose: one mark instance is referenced by the declaration, by its projected legend entry, and by every merged legend downstream — the sharing is only safe because nothing can write to it, and that is a property of the type rather than of anyone's care
tests/test_config.py.body: Construct a provisional mark, then assign to its claim. The assignment raises. The same holds for its revisit condition. Assigning a new attribute that was never declared also raises.

tests/test_config.py.title: `RunConfig()` constructs with no arguments and no field anywhere in the tree is absent
tests/test_config.py.purpose: completeness has to hold recursively — a nested section with a field lacking a default constructs fine at the top level only if the section itself was given a default instance, and the failure then surfaces as an absent value much further downstream
tests/test_config.py.body: Construct the run configuration with no arguments. It succeeds. Walking its fields recursively into every nested section, every field has a value; no field is absent, unset, or a placeholder sentinel object standing for absence. Reading any field of any nested section by attribute succeeds.

tests/test_config.py.title: A resolved configuration refuses to be written back to, at every level of the tree
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the top-level object being frozen is the easy half; a nested section declared without the same guard is the gap, and a consumer that recomputed a value and wrote it into a section would produce a value that governed the run and appears in no record
tests/test_config.py.body: Construct a run configuration and assign to one of its top-level fields. The assignment raises. Assign to a field of a nested section reached through it. That assignment raises too, and this holds for every nested section in the tree, not only the outermost object.

tests/test_config.py.title: A setting the document never mentions is present in the resolved configuration at its declared default
tests/test_config.py.purpose: resolution walks the schema, not the document; a resolver written the other way round passes every test that supplies a full document and returns an object with holes the moment one is partial
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document that states one setting inside one table and mentions no other table at all. The result is a complete configuration: the stated setting carries the authored value, and every other setting in every other table carries its declared default. An entirely empty document resolves to a configuration equal to the one constructed with no arguments.

tests/test_config.py.title: A key matching no declared setting is refused, and the message names its dotted path
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the silent-ignore failure is the expensive one: the run uses the default while the author reads their document and believes otherwise, and nothing in the stored record ever disagrees with them
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document containing a key that matches no declared setting. Resolution raises the configuration error, and the message contains the dotted path of the offending key. This holds for an unrecognised key at the top level, for one inside a recognised table, and for an entire table that matches no declared section — including a key that is a near-miss spelling of a real setting.

tests/test_config.py.title: A value whose type differs from the declared field's is refused, and the message names its dotted path
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the near-misses are what slip through: an integer where a float is declared, a string that looks like a number, a single value where a sequence is declared
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document supplying a string for a setting declared as a number. Resolution raises the configuration error naming that setting's dotted path. The same holds for a value supplied where a nested table is declared, and for a scalar supplied where a sequence is declared.

tests/test_config.py.title: A value its setting's check rejects is refused, and the message quotes the declared unit and admissible text
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the message being projected from the declaration rather than written beside it is the point — a hand-written error message is a second copy of the admissibility that drifts from the check the moment the bound moves
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document supplying, for a setting whose admissible values exclude it, a value of the correct type that the setting's check rejects. Resolution raises the configuration error. The message contains that setting's dotted path, the unit text as declared, and the admissible text as declared, character for character rather than paraphrased.

tests/test_config.py.title: A resolved configuration survives the round trip through its document form unchanged
tests/test_config.py.purpose: this is the property that makes a sealed record re-executable months later; a lossy emission is invisible until someone tries to reproduce a result and gets a slightly different one
tests/test_config.py.body: Take a configuration in which several settings across several tables hold non-default values, including a sequence-valued setting and a nested table. Emit it as a document and resolve that document. The result equals the configuration it came from. The emitted document contains only plain mappings, sequences and primitive values — nothing that would not survive being written out and read back.

tests/test_config.py.title: The emitted document carries every declared setting, including ones the author never stated
tests/test_config.py.purpose: an emission that skips settings left at their default still round-trips, because resolution fills them back in — so the round-trip check alone cannot catch it, and the stored record would then not say what value governed the run
tests/test_config.py.body: Emit a document from a configuration constructed with no arguments. Every declared setting in every table is present in that document with the value it took. No setting is omitted on the grounds that it was left at its default.

tests/test_config.py.title: A configuration loaded from a TOML file resolves to the same object as the same document resolved directly
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the binary-versus-text reading mode is the recurring papercut of this module, and it fails as a type error on the parse rather than as a wrong value, so it is cheap to pin once
tests/test_config.py.body: Write a TOML document to a file, load the configuration from that path, and separately parse the same text and resolve the resulting mapping. The two configurations are equal. Loading a file whose content is not valid TOML raises, and loading a valid file whose content states an unrecognised key raises the configuration error, with the dotted path in the message as for a directly resolved document.

tests/test_config.py.title: An omitted setting whose default its own admissibility check refuses is refused by its dotted path
tests/test_config.py.purpose: without this the sentinel doctrine is decorative: a document stating nothing resolves to a structurally complete configuration whose estimation cadence is zero, whose variant is the empty string and whose fallback policy nobody declared, and the first symptom is a division by zero inside a stepping loop rather than a refusal at load
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document that omits a setting whose declared default its own admissibility check returns false for. Resolution is refused and the refusal names that setting's dotted path. This holds wherever such a setting is declared — the refusal follows from the default failing its own check, not from the path appearing on any list the resolver consults, so a setting given such a default is refused with nothing else declared anywhere. Supplying an admissible value for that path in the document resolves without complaint.

tests/test_config.py.title: The refusal for an omitted setting says the document supplied no value, and quotes the declaration's own unit and admissible text
tests/test_config.py.purpose: a reader told only that a value is inadmissible goes hunting for a value they never wrote, which is the whole of the wasted time here; and the text has to be projected from the declaration rather than authored beside the raise, or the message and the declaration are two statements of one fact and will disagree
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document that omits a setting whose default its own check refuses. The refusal names the dotted path, carries the setting's declared unit and its declared admissible text word for word as the declaration states them, and states that the document supplied no value at that path. Resolve a document that instead supplies an inadmissible value at the same path: the refusal carries the same path, unit and admissible text, and says that the supplied value was refused rather than that the path was absent. Editing the declaration's admissible text changes both messages with nothing else edited.

tests/test_config.py.title: An omitted setting whose default its own check accepts resolves to that default silently
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the rule is that a supplied default is checked, not that it is distrusted — a resolver that refused every omission would satisfy every sentinel observation beside this one and would quietly make the entire configuration surface mandatory, so this is the observation that separates checking defaults from rejecting them
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document that omits a setting whose declared default its own check accepts. Resolution succeeds, the field holds the declared default, and no refusal and no diagnostic is produced for that path. Resolve an empty document against a declaration tree in which every default is accepted by its own check: resolution succeeds and the result equals the tree constructed with no arguments.

tests/test_config.py.title: A resolved configuration survives the round trip through its document form unchanged
tests/test_config.py.purpose: the property has to be exercised from a configuration the resolver returned, never from one constructed with no arguments — a configuration of sentinels emits a document that will not resolve, so writing the round trip the obvious way produces a test that fails for the right reason and reads as a defect in the resolver, and that misreading is how the defaults-are-checked rule gets reverted
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve an admissible document into a configuration. Emit a document from that configuration and resolve it again: the result equals the configuration it came from, every setting included, and the emitted document carries every declared setting with the value its field took. The property is stated over configurations resolution can return, which is what the round trip is about; a document emitted from a configuration constructed with no arguments carries values their own checks refuse and is therefore refused when resolved, by dotted path, rather than round-tripping.

tests/test_config.py.title: An omitted topology and an omitted mission phase list are not refused at load
tests/test_config.py.purpose: these are the omissions the load-time rule deliberately does not catch, because each is admissible only against a sibling field and a per-value check sees one value — the tempting repair is to widen the check so one field can read another, which would put structural predicates inside the declaration primitive and duplicate a refusal that already exists elsewhere; the cost is that these two omissions are refused later than the rest, and that is the contract rather than an oversight
tests/test_config.py.body: Resolve a document that declares no topology and no mission phases. Resolution succeeds: both arrangements resolve to their empty defaults and the phase list resolves empty, with no refusal naming either path, because each empty value satisfies every clause of its own admissibility that a single value can decide. Resolving the same document is refused if it omits a setting whose default its own check refuses, so the two omissions are distinguished by whether the declared default is admissible on its own and by nothing else.

audit.rule: any file touched outside editable_paths is a write this unit never declared, and is almost always a dependency nobody declared. Files inside it may be shared with the units named in `overlap`, which is why those must not be worked at the same time -- but each of them declares the file too, so a write here is still within this unit's own write set
